key_figure_caption: Three arrangements correcting the fundamental-harmonic phase mismatch: crystal replaced by its inversion image every distance delta (ZnS), multiple total reflections in quartz, resonant interferometer cavity.
key_figure_reason: the phase-correction (periodic inversion) scheme behind the paper's QPM significance
notes: Received 1962-04-16 (p.1). Physical Review vol. 127 no. 6, 15 September 1962, pp.1918-1939 (= text.md pp.1-22). Byline J. A. Armstrong, N. Bloembergen, J. Ducuing, P. S. Pershan; Ducuing footnoted as on leave from the Departement de Physique Appliquee, Cie Gle de Telegraphie sans fil (Orsay), France, O.E.E.C. fellow 1961 (p.1, not added to orgs_printed). era: E1 1960-1969 laser, nonlinear optics, integrated-optics idea
event: Coherent infrared emission from forward-biased GaAs p-n junctions; threshold near 8500 A/cm2, narrowing 125 to 15 Angstrom; claimed first solid-state electrical-to-coherent conversion.
event_locator: p.1 abstract paragraph; p.2; p.3 'first time' claim
orgs_printed: General Electric Research Laboratory, Schenectady, New York
key_figure_caption: Emission spectra of diode L-69 below and above threshold, about 8200-8700 Angstrom, with different vertical scales; above threshold a narrow line near 8400 Angstrom.
key_figure_reason: spectral narrowing beyond threshold, one of the three coherence proofs
notes: Received 1962-09-24 (p.1). Physical Review Letters vol. 9 no. 9, 1 November 1962, pp.366-368 (= text.md pp.1-3); the lower half of p.3 is the next letter (van Roggen, polymer crystals), text.md p.4 is an unrelated image. Scan with a text layer: numbers read from page_01.png - page_03.png. 'first' claim (p.3): the authors state this is the first time direct conversion of electrical energy to coherent infrared radiation has been achieved in a solid state device, and the first laser with transitions between energy bands. Byline R. N. Hall, G. E. Fenner, J. D. Kingsley, T. J. Soltys, R. O. Carlson; no individual roles stated, papers.csv DRI (Hall, audit basis) kept. No acknowledgment section. Fig. 1 (p.1) shows the radiation patterns (vertical interference bands above threshold); Fig. 3 (p.2) spectra of diode L-70 at four current densities.

era: E1 1960-1969 laser, nonlinear optics, integrated-optics idea
event: Coherent visible emission near 7100 Angstrom from forward-biased Ga(As1-xPx) p-n junctions at 77 K: threshold about 11,000 A/cm2, line narrowing 125 to 12 Angstrom.
orgs_printed: Advanced Semiconductor Laboratory, Semiconductor Products Department, General Electric Company, Syracuse, N. Y.
key_figure_caption: Emission spectra of Ga(As1-xPx) diode 28A at 77 K: below threshold (11,000 A/cm2, about 125 Angstrom wide) and above threshold (19,000 A/cm2, about 12 Angstrom), peak near 7100 Angstrom.
key_figure_reason: the only figure; shows the visible-wavelength line narrowing
notes: Received 1962-10-17 (p.2). Applied Physics Letters vol. 1 no. 4, 1 December 1962, pp.82-83 (= text.md pp.2-3); text.md p.1 is a publisher download cover sheet. Read from img_p02_1.png (full-page scan of p.2) and page_03.png. The paper calls the emission 'coherent (visible)' and does not claim 'first'. Byline Nick Holonyak, Jr. and S. F. Bevacqua; acknowledgment (p.3) credits C. V. Bielan, F. A. Carranti, B. G. Hess, S. J. Lubowski with substantial contributions to fabrication of the junctions, J. D. Kingsley with spectral measurements, G. E. Fenner with threshold and radiation-pattern measurements, and R. N. Hall with discussions and contributions; DRI unchanged. Supported in part by the Air Force Cambridge Research Laboratories (p.3).

orgs_printed: Central Research Lab., Varian Associates, Palo Alto, Calif.
key_figure_caption: Band diagram of the heterojunction laser structure under forward bias: wide-gap n+ and p+ injectors around a narrow-gap base, electron and hole quasi-Fermi levels.
key_figure_reason: the only figure of the letter; defines the proposed double-heterojunction structure
notes: Received 1963-10-14 (p.1 footnote of this letter, read from page_01.png; the 'Received October 9, 1963' in text.md belongs to the preceding Slobodin letter). Proceedings of the IEEE Correspondence, December 1963, pp.1782-1783; the volume number is not printed on these pages. text.md p.1 interleaves this letter with the preceding 'Optical Correlation Technique' letter (Slobodin, Lockheed Electronics; its Fig. 1-5); this letter starts in col. 3 of p.1. Key figure from page_02.png (img_p02_1.png is the full-page scan).

event: Locks the modes of a 0.633-um He-Ne laser by intracavity acoustic loss modulation at the round-trip frequency, about 56 Mc/s; 2.5-ns pulses observed.
dri_locator: p.2 byline (first of three authors, L. E. Hargrove)
orgs_printed: Bell Telephone Laboratories, Incorporated, Murray Hill, New Jersey
key_figure_caption: Scanning-interferometer display of a typical locked optical mode spectrum: light intensity versus optical frequency, a stationary comb of modes.
key_figure_reason: the measured locked mode spectrum; Fig. 1 is only the setup
notes: Received 1964-05-11 (p.2). Applied Physics Letters vol. 5 no. 1, 1 July 1964, pp.4-5 (= text.md pp.2-3); text.md p.1 is a publisher cover sheet and the lower half of p.3 starts the companion letter by Fork, Hargrove and Pollack. The paper does not claim 'first'; it notes DiDomenico independently predicted the locking (p.2). Byline L. E. Hargrove, R. L. Fork, M. A. Pollack; no individual roles stated, papers.csv DRI kept. Cavity length printed as '~ 2.66' with the unit illegible in the scan (p.2). Pulse halfwidth 2.5 ns with repetition period about 17.8 ns, locking range about 1e-5 c/2L (p.3). Fig. 1 (p.2) is the setup with the fused-quartz acoustic modulator near the end mirror.
